text: . It has been used as a preservative in cosmetics and topical pharmaceuticals at a concentration of 0.5 to 1%. It is often used with other preservatives, commonly hydroxybenzoates, to obtain a wider spectrum of antimicrobial activity. Phenoxyethanol is used in concentrations of about 2% as an an- tiseptic for minor infections of skin, wounds, and mucous mem- branes. Aqueous solutions may be prepared by shaking the phe- noxyethanol with hot water until dissolved, then adjusting to final volume when cool. Preparation of the solution can be aided by propylene glycol. Phenoxypropanol and chlorophenoxyethanol are related com- pounds used in topical preparations.
